originalTitle: CIO 正在抛弃 AI 生码率：一场关于什么才算产研提效的实践复盘
title: CIOs Are Abandoning AI Code Generation Rate: A Practical Review of What Truly Counts as R&D Efficiency
oneSentenceSummary: Based on a year of practical experience, the Alibaba Cloud CIO team proposes that the core of R&D efficiency in the AI era lies in 'scaling' rather than 'code generation rate.' By implementing left-shifted quality testing, knowledge engineering, API specifications, and Half-Stack role restructuring, they achieved a 3x increase in effective code output per frontend developer, 2x for backend developers, and a 30%-55% reduction in defect rates.
summary: This article is an in-depth review by Alibaba Cloud CIO Jiang Linquan and his team on scaling R&D organizational efficiency in the AI era. It first identifies two popular misconceptions: AI code generation rate as a process metric easily leads to 'padding,' and Vibe Coding is difficult to directly implement in existing enterprise systems. The core argument is that once code is produced, it is primarily a liability; scaling efficiency should focus on business value, not code volume. Through AI assistance, the team achieved four major left-shifts: quality and test coverage increased from 20% to nearly 100%; knowledge engineering and spec restoration for existing systems; API First specifications to end system 'compensation'; and Vibe Coding used for upfront requirement clarification. Organizationally, they abandoned the full-stack engineer fantasy, restructuring into two Half-Stack roles: PDFE (AI Product Design Frontend Engineer) and ABE (AI Architecture Backend Engineer), significantly reducing collaboration chains. The final framework is a trinity of 'Product Value Guidance × Engineering Efficiency × Organizational Change.' The article also explores the difficulty of realizing Agent value, the difference between individual and organizational efficiency gains, and the scarce skills in the AI era—a return to the fundamentals of language and mathematics, and judgment driven by taste.
featuredReason: This InfoQ piece challenges the popular AI code generation rate metric by examining real CIO decisions and ground-level implementation cases. It argues for more meaningful productivity measures and offers a practical evaluation framework for teams adopting AI coding tools in engineering workflows.

mainPoints.point: AI code generation rate is a dangerous process metric; focus on E2E measurement of business value.
mainPoints.explanation: Code lines are meaningless without weighting, and AI code generation rate can easily trap teams in a 'padding' pitfall. Actual coding accounts for only 20% of the software engineering lifecycle. Even if AI achieves a 70%-80% code generation rate for easy-to-write code, the overall end-to-end efficiency improvement remains limited.

mainPoints.point: Vibe Coding is not suitable for direct production use; it should serve as a tool for upfront requirement clarification.
mainPoints.explanation: Core enterprise applications are mostly existing systems, and code generated by Vibe Coding cannot directly assume production quality responsibility. However, it can be used to quickly generate prototypes, allowing business stakeholders to confirm requirements at the earliest stage via live demos, reducing misunderstandings and rework from the source.

mainPoints.point: AI rewrites the classic challenges of the 'Mythical Man-Month' and 'Engineering Left-Shift.'
mainPoints.explanation: Adding an AI Agent is different from adding a person. Agents can access context without loss, avoiding the geometric increase in communication overhead. AI can extract knowledge assets from existing code, reducing the organizational friction and cost of left-shifting, making quality left-shift from 'correct but expensive' to executable.

mainPoints.point: Organizations should abandon the full-stack fantasy and restructure into two Half-Stack roles: PDFE and ABE.
mainPoints.explanation: Full-stack talent is scarce and difficult to recruit. Companies should leverage AI to lower cross-domain barriers. PDFE merges product managers, interaction designers, and frontend engineers, while ABE integrates architecture design, backend development, and AI Agent development. The two collaborate via API contracts, significantly compressing the collaboration chain.

mainPoints.point: The scarce capability in the AI era is 'taste'—the judgment to define problems and manage Agents.
mainPoints.explanation: Skills are inflating; judgment of business value (taste) is the scarce resource. Foundational abilities return to language (precise understanding and expression) and mathematics (lossless abstraction), while higher-level abilities involve defining the leftmost problem and managing Agent teams.

keyQuotes: Once code is produced, it is first and foremost a liability. The large amount of added code 'may' be an asset, but it is 'definitely' a liability.
AI code generation rate is a 'process metric.' Once an organization observes such a process metric, AI can easily become toxic.
Taste is the judgment of business value, the final acceptance criterion for whether something is good or bad. AI can only achieve average, but people with taste can define what 'good' is.

Essentially, taste is the crystallization of human experience, abstract ability, and sense of responsibility in a complex world. AI can raise the floor, but the ceiling will always be defined by humans.
